# CHANGELOG-PENDING

Unreleased changes to be curated into the next `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

**Instructions for contributors:** add a one-line entry under the appropriate section when your PR introduces a user-visible change. PR number in brackets at the end. Entries are curated (not auto-generated) before each release.

Format: `- Brief description of what changed. ([#NNN])`

---

## Added

- ag2-sparrow (Codex): `ag2-sparrow-codex view` follows what a Codex agent is doing, read-only. Codex runs as a background app-server with no terminal to attach to, so its connector now writes each turn as plain lines to `state/live-view.log` under the agent's work root (who the turn is for, the agent's words as they arrive, each command, file change and tool call with its outcome, how the turn ended), and `view` prints the end of that log and then every new line. The log is private to the user, cut to 2000 characters a line, and starts over with its last 100 KB past 1 MB. A view that cannot be written never fails a turn. The module (`live_view`) is shared, for the other connectors that have no terminal.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): `ag2-sparrow-antigravity-local view` follows what a local Antigravity (`agy acp`) agent is doing, read-only, as `ag2-sparrow-codex view` does for Codex. The connector writes each turn to the same `state/live-view.log` through the shared `live_view` module: who the turn is for, agy's words as they arrive, each tool call (the command it runs, the files it changes, else its title; `pending` until that call reports `completed`, `failed` when it fails, so a refused call is never shown as done), each permission decision (allowed or refused, with the policy's reason), and how the turn ended. The prompt's framing, environment and MCP setup are never written. The connector writes the view off the ACP reader thread (bounded queue, overflow counted) and only to a regular file. `acp_host.run_prompt` takes the view as an optional `view=`; OpenClaw passes none and is unchanged.
<!-- feat() PRs go here -->
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): local Codex now works like local Claude Code and the Codex core's seat: one shared thread for the owner's and attested collaborators' turns from every room, instead of one thread per room, still one turn at a time. Its id is kept in `state/thread` (0600) and resumed after an app-server restart; a thread that cannot be resumed is replaced by a new shared thread and logged. Each prompt on it opens with its room, its sender and that the reply goes back to that room (a collaborator keeps the non-owner note); replies are still routed by task, and a model pick applies to that thread in every room. `install --resume-thread` never becomes the shared thread: the owner's conversation is carried into an owner-only thread (`state/owner-thread`, 0600) that only the owner's DM turns continue, as before, and the shared thread starts fresh; a saved shared thread that is an owner-only conversation (the `--resume-thread` id, the owner-only thread, or an earlier version's owner-only room thread) is replaced by a fresh shared thread and logged; `--thread-id THREAD` seeds the shared thread while none is saved; the older `--thread-id CHANNEL_ID=THREAD` named one owner channel's own thread and is never resumed as the shared thread (a fresh one starts, and the channel is logged). Guests, plain team and unattested collaborator claims keep their own ephemeral thread with integrations off. Per-room thread files under `state/threads/` are left in place, unused. Sharing with collaborators can be turned off: `install --no-allow-collaborator` (recorded as `ALLOW_COLLABORATOR=0`, shown by `verify`) serves attested collaborators as guests, each turn on its own ephemeral read-only thread with integrations off, never the shared thread or `--resume-thread`; a repair, the desktop's move after an update and a reinstall without the flag keep the opt-out, and only `--allow-collaborator` turns sharing back on. Repair lines printed after a failed install now carry `--no-allow-non-owner` and `--no-allow-collaborator` as bare flags (they used to print `--allow-non-owner 0 --no-allow-non-owner 0`, which install refused).
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): Antigravity now works like local Claude Code: one long-lived `agy acp` process and one shared Session for the owner's and attested collaborators' turns from every room (the AG2 Space tools attached once; each prompt starts with its room, its sender and that the reply goes back to that room; a collaborator gets the same non-owner note), still one turn at a time. The Session id is kept in `state/shared-session.json` (0600) and resumed after a restart; agy is restarted when it exited, a request timed out, a sign-in or quota error hit, or the app's Gemini API key was saved, replaced (A to B) or removed (seen in this agent's own Keychain item's attributes, read without the key: the version a newer app sets on each write, else the item's dates; the marker kept for a process is the one read on both sides of its own authenticate, and none when that start could not read the key itself (a key read but refused by agy keeps it, on the sign-in); a failed query is unknown and restarts nothing, except that a process started while unknown, or while the key moved, is restarted once when the marker reads again; after a start that could not read the key, that restart waits for the marker to move or for a backoff of 60 s, doubling to 30 min while the key stays unreadable, so a Keychain that keeps refusing the key does not restart agy each turn), and a turn not yet sent is tried once more; a Session opened under the other sign-in mode, or one agy will not load, is replaced and logged. Guests, plain team and unattested collaborator claims keep a throwaway Session in a short process of their own, with no tools, never saved. A model pick the Session does not list is no longer sent (agy refused it with "Unknown model ID"): the owner is told once and the pick is kept. `--shared-session-turns N` (default off) starts a new shared Session after N turns. `install --no-allow-collaborator` opts collaborators out: they are then served as guests are, never the shared Session; the choice is kept by every reinstall (repair, token reinstall, the app's update) unless `--allow-collaborator` is given. Old per-room Sessions are left in place, unused. ([#6922])
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): a local Codex agent gets the S.space room tools (the `ag2-space` MCP server) acting as the agent itself, as antigravity-local does, so it can post in rooms on its own and @-mention people. `install --mcp-proxy-command "'<node>' '<engine>/ag2-mcp-proxy.mjs'"` records `MCP_PROXY_COMMAND` (same check and quoting as antigravity-local; listed in `--help`); with the agent's own `--token-env-file`, only the owner-only thread (`state/owner-thread`, which only the owner's DM turns run on and which never becomes the shared thread) starts or resumes with `mcp_servers.ag2-space`: the desktop's stdio proxy under the name shim, which lists and forwards only the granted room tools, given only a 0600 descriptor naming the agent's token file, so no token enters Codex's config or environment. The shared thread, which collaborators' turns and the owner's room turns run on, is never opened with the tools, and no turn on it gets the grant or the prompt hint; an owner's DM with no owner-only conversation to continue runs on the shared thread, so without them. A resume refused or timed out with the tools continues the same conversation without them. The tools stay off unless the owner is the only one served: both `--no-allow-collaborator` and `--no-allow-non-owner` must be set (the install defaults serve both, so a default install gets none), and a setting that is missing or unreadable counts as serving them; the refusal comes before any config read or token exchange, and `install` prints a note. They also need an owner-only conversation that already exists (`--resume-thread`, or a kept `state/owner-thread`). Existing installs and the shared-thread defaults are unchanged. Plain team and guest turns are unchanged (their own ephemeral thread, every MCP server off). An install without the option keeps working with no tools; one whose Codex config already has an `ag2-space` entry is left as it is. The stdio entry helpers move to a shared `ag2_sparrow/mcp_stdio.py` that both connectors import. Codex keeps a thread's MCP server between turns, so the shim forwards a tool call only under a live per-turn grant (`state/ag2-mcp-grant.json`, 0600: the thread's launch id, the tools, an expiry) that the connector writes when an owner's turn starts and removes when it ends; between turns, on another thread, after expiry, or in an attested collaborator's turn (no grant until the tools enforce a collaborator's rooms and actions) every call is refused, and a grant file that is not a JSON object allows nothing. A saved conversation whose resume Codex refuses with the `ag2-space` entry is resumed again without it (that thread runs without the tools) before a new thread replaces it.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): a local Claude Code agent gets the S.space room tools (the `ag2-space` MCP server) acting as the agent itself, as codex-local and antigravity-local do, so it can post in rooms on its own and @-mention people. `install --mcp-proxy-command "'<node>' '<engine>/ag2-mcp-proxy.mjs'"` records `MCP_PROXY_COMMAND` (same check and quoting; listed in `--help` of install and connect; kept on a repair reinstall). With the agent's own token file, each start of the session (a restart after a sign-in change too) writes the 0600 descriptor and a 0600 `--mcp-config` file under `state/room-tools/` naming one stdio server, the desktop's proxy under the name shim granting the owner's room tools, and passes `--mcp-config` to the session; no token reaches Claude Code's argv, environment or config. The agent's other MCP servers keep working (no `--strict-mcp-config`); one whose Claude Code config already has an `ag2-space` server keeps it and gets none of ours. A conf without the option, a missing token file or a failed token exchange (bounded at 12 s) starts the session without the tools. Restricted senders' isolated `claude -p` turn is unchanged: no MCP server at all. The tools are a preview the owner turns on with `install --room-tools-preview` (recorded as `ROOM_TOOLS_PREVIEW`, kept on a repair); the proxy command alone, which the desktop app passes at install and update, changes nothing for an agent or its collaborators. So "the desktop app passes the proxy" (wired) and "this agent has the tools" (enabled) are two different things: an agent is enabled only once its owner installs it with the preview, and installing it again without the preview leaves the tools' conversation (once its process is proven gone) for the earlier one, or a new one when there was none, without the tools: the conversation that held the tools' results stays on disk and is never the one collaborators share. With the preview on, the tools are the owner's only. Install starts a new conversation for them (`ROOM_TOOLS_SESSION`) and says what that costs a collaborator; the earlier one stays on disk (`EARLIER_SESSION_ID`) and never gets the tools, nor does a conversation the owner names with `--resume-session`, nor a session whose old process is not proven gone (the command says to stop the job and install again). Only the owner's tasks are submitted to the tools' session: an attested collaborator's task is then answered on the turn of its own that restricted senders get (no session, no tools), where it used to share the owner's session. Which session has the tools is read from the running process (a mark `hold` writes for the process it starts with them, before it runs), never from the install config, for admission and for the shim's check alike; a mark that cannot be read keeps collaborators out. Before each `tools/call` the shim runs the adapter's `inbox room-tools` check and forwards the call only in that session while a turn of the owner's is confirmed and not yet answered; a check that exits non-zero, or anything it cannot read, refuses. A recorded proxy whose executable is gone (an app update moved it) is logged at session start and offers no tools.
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): the owner adds a Codex account to a local Codex agent from their phone. "Add account" on the agent's account card (owner, owner's DM, a card this agent posted in the last 5 minutes) runs Codex's own device-code sign-in (`codex login --device-auth`) into a staging Codex home; the card shows the link (its domain spelled out) and the one-time code, and nothing is pasted back. When the sign-in completes the card asks "Signed in as <email>. Use this account for Codex?": only Yes moves it into the agent's own Codex home, and the agent keeps its current account until then; No, or no answer in 5 minutes, signs the staged login out and deletes it. One sign-in at a time per agent, first answer only, ended after 5 minutes; a "Sign out" button signs the agent's own home out. Refused for an agent with no Codex home of its own, `~/.codex`, or a home shared with the core or another agent.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): the account card in the owner's DM also offers "Use <address>" for each account the desktop app already saved for this agent on this computer (read from the app's `accounts/claude-local/<agent key>/index.json`, labels only; the account in use left out, at most five, by address), so the account can be switched from a phone. A tap, only the owner's, in their DM, on a card this agent posted that offered that account, asks the app to switch (`.ag2-switch-request.json`, v2, 0600, created exclusively; one switch at a time per agent, a second tap meanwhile is told "A switch is already running") and shows "Switching to <address>…" in place of the card, then "Switched to <address>" or "Could not switch: <why>" from the app's per-request receipt. The contract (v2): the app claims the request by renaming it to `.ag2-switch-claimed-<nonce>.json` and answers in `.ag2-switch-result-<nonce>.json`; a switch whose new sign-in the app has not tried yet (`verified` false or absent) says so ("if the next reply fails, sign in again"), and an outcome that is not known (the app restarted mid-switch, `unknown`; a receipt that is not an answer of the contract's shape) says which account the agent is on now, never "Could not switch". Only the app releases a claim (it answers one it left at its next launch): a claim unanswered 15 minutes is told once as not known yet ("if the app on that computer was closed or crashed, opening it again will finish this"), and its answer is still shown when it comes ("… after all"); until then a tap is told a previous switch is unresolved. A request file that is not a whole request and is over 2 minutes old no longer blocks a switch and is removed while unchanged. If the other agents' configs cannot all be listed and read, no switch is offered or made. The watchers' log (`state/account-remote.log`) is owner-only. A request the app has not picked up in 90 s is withdrawn and said so ("Nothing was changed"); one it is still working on is said in progress, never failed, and a result that comes after the watcher stopped waiting (10 min) is told on the next card or tap; a watcher ended by a restart is started again. Refused, in one line, for an agent with no config dir of its own, one that is the core's, the person's or another agent's, and one behind the credential proxy.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local, antigravity-local): the owner's short message in their DM asking which account or model the agent is on, or to change it, shows the card in Chinese, English or the two mixed ("你在用什么模型", "what model are you using", "什么 account"), not only a fixed list of phrasings; asking about the account and the model together ("你在用哪个账号和模型") shows both cards. One shared matcher (`ag2_sparrow/card_ask.py`); a longer message, or one about some other account ("create an account on GitHub"), still goes to the model.
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): when the signed-in account cannot use the model a turn asked for (a model picked on another account), the owner's DM gets the model card ("<model> isn't available on this account. Pick one it has.") instead of "Codex ended this task with status failed", and the message waits: it is answered, on the pick, as soon as the owner picks. It waits only for a refusal that came before the turn did anything, only in the owner's DM, at most 10 minutes, and only once; if the owner writes on in that DM instead, it is answered first. Anywhere else, or when no card can be shown, the reply says the account can't use that model and where to pick one. ([#6823])
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): `/account` or `/login` in the owner's DM (or the session answering `[account-card]`) shows an account card: the agent's Anthropic account and, in the desktop app on the computer that runs the agent, the controls to switch it right in the card (`account_controls`); a sign-in code never travels in chat. When the session hits its usage limit (Claude Code's own limit menu is the live dialog on its screen, at startup or mid-turn) or runs out of credits, the owner gets that card unasked in their DM, once per limit, with when it resets if the screen says; every owner message left unanswered behind the menu gets it once. Words that only read like a limit (a reply, a quoted message, an old banner) send no card. Nothing is typed into the session.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): the owner changes the session's model from their DM, by the same model card as Antigravity and local Codex. `/model` in the DM shows the card (Default, Opus, Sonnet 1M, Haiku, Fable 1M); a tap, `/model <name>`, or the owner's own words ("switch to haiku") switch the running session live, with no restart, once it is out of a task's turn, and the card says whether it took and why not. Asked in other words, the session answers with `[model-card]` and the card is shown. Taps and `/model` are answered by `inbox claim` and never reach the session; any tap but the owner's in their DM is refused. The isolated turn for a restricted sender runs on the same pick. A work root that had used `model` or a card no longer refuses to start (`state/model-switch.json`, `state/agent-cards` and the cards' other records are now this adapter's state).
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): the account card says "I'm using <full email>. Switch this agent's account below." (no plan suffix) and carries `account_controls`, so the desktop app draws the agent's saved accounts and sign-in in the card; when Codex is out of usage (its `usageLimitExceeded` turn error, or a used-up `account/rateLimits` window, never an error's wording) the connector posts that card on its own in the owner's DM, once per limit, with the reset time when Codex gave one, and a refused turn posts no error line while it is out; a turn refused as `unauthorized` restarts the app-server on the login on disk, and is run once more only when it had not done anything (one that had started work is never run again); still signed out, the owner gets the account card. Moving to another account's sign-in is the sign-in check's ([#6782]). A task the bridge archived mid-turn no longer crashes the card step, and Codex is no longer told to write `results/<task>.txt` itself. ([#6821])
- ag2-sparrow (connector cards): what a tap on a model or account card comes to is shown in place of the card tapped (the bridge sends it as an edit of that message), not as a second card: "Switching to X", then "Switched" or "could not switch"; the sign-in page, then how the sign-in ended; a tap on a card that no longer acts gets the fresh card in its place. A card asked for in words (`/model`, `/account`) is still a new card, and an edit the server refuses is posted as a new card. Antigravity and local Codex.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local): when the account a local agent is signed in with changes (a sign-in from the app, or the desktop's switch marker), its CLI is restarted so the next turn runs on the new account: local Claude Code once the current turn ends (at once only when the session sits on the usage-limit menu itself) and its input box is empty, so an unsent draft is never typed over; local Codex by restarting its app-server before the next turn, also when the new account carries the same email, and a restart that fails is tried again without stopping task service.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local): when the account a local agent is signed in with changes (a sign-in from the app, or the desktop's switch marker), its CLI is restarted so the next turn runs on the new account: local Claude Code once the current turn ends (at once only when the session sits on the usage-limit menu itself) and its input box is empty, so an unsent draft is never typed over; local Codex by restarting its app-server before the next turn, also when the new account carries the same email. No prompt is sent under an account other than the one selected: while a server cannot be started on it, the running one is kept but gets no prompt, the first sender is told at once in plain words to send again, later messages wait and are answered once it starts or, after 30 seconds of waiting, are told the same without anyone having to write again, and task service never stops. After a switch was seen, a sign-in file that cannot be read (mid-write) is never taken for a match: turns wait until it reads.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): `ag2-sparrow-claude-local account` prints the Anthropic account of the agent's Claude config dir (address masked), and `account --switch` signs that dir in again with Claude Code's own sign-in, which opens the browser of that computer (`--console` for a Console account). No API key is involved. It is refused for an agent with no config dir of its own (that would change the person's own login) and for one whose session goes through the credential proxy, whose own sign-in decides the account. A new sign-in applies when the session next starts. For an owner who is not at that computer the sign-in also runs in two steps: `account --start` prints the link of the sign-in page and waits 10 minutes, `account --code` reads the code that page showed from standard input and finishes it (`--cancel` ends it); a wrong code is refused in Claude Code's own words, and the command writes the code nowhere (the message it came in stays in that conversation; Claude Code treats the code as single-use, which is not independently tested). A sign-in (`--start`, `--code`, `--switch`) runs only with a terminal on its input: by hand, or from the app's Settings, which run the command under one and take the code in the app's own box. An agent's own shell has no terminal, so no message in a room, whoever sent it, can have the agent sign in, and a sign-in link or code never passes through a chat. This is not a boundary against someone who already has this user's shell. A sign-in is refused for a config dir that is the person's own, the Sutando core's or another agent's. An agent behind the credential proxy is refused when the command can see that (the agent's own run); run at a terminal it cannot see the session's environment, so it signs in and says that the proxy's sign-in decides the account if the session uses one.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): when agy is not signed in, the owner's DM gets a card whose sign-in the desktop app draws in place (`account_controls`, `signed_out`), instead of the line telling them to run `agy acp --login` in a terminal; elsewhere, or when the card cannot be queued, the line stays. ([#6802])
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): an account card in the owner's DM ("switch account" / "use API key", in English or Chinese, or `/account`), in English, with "Switch account" and "Use API key": it carries `account_controls`, so the desktop app on the computer that runs the agent switches account or takes a key right in the card (no code or key is taken in chat, and one sent there is never passed to agy), and "Stop using API key"; the turn after a switch says which account agy now uses (from agy's own log); a quota error (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, a 429) makes the connector post the account card on its own in the owner's DM, once per limit (the next only after a turn answered and the limit came back), saying when it resets if agy said and the account in use; while it is out a refused turn posts no error line. Owner only. ([#6713])
- quota-tracker: Claude Code quota is tracked without the credential proxy. Every Claude session launch (the core and each pool worker) installs a status line recorder and a `StopFailure` (`rate_limit`) hook in that session's config dir, which write `state/quota-state.json` in the proxy's shape with `source: "statusline"` (`src/quota_record.py`; newest observation wins). The top level is the core's login; other logins' latest are kept under `accounts` and never change the core's numbers or status. A status line already there is kept and its output shown unchanged. On by default; `QUOTA_STATUSLINE_ENABLED=false` in the skill's manifest config removes it and puts the old status line back. Health-check no longer warns about a stopped proxy when the record comes from the status line, and warns when that record stops moving while the core works. Skills get a new manifest field, `on_session_config`, run once per Claude session launch with the session's config dir. With the recorder on, the core and pool workers now call Anthropic directly: the launchers and `src/startup.sh` stop setting, and drop, an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` that points at the local credential proxy (an owner-set base URL is kept). This is the default after upgrading, with no fallback to the proxy. If a session's config dir is not signed in on its own (it only ever worked through the proxy), you are asked to sign in: health-check's `claude-sign-in` row fails and your DM gets one message a day with the exact command, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR='<config dir>' claude auth login`. Each session then uses its own config dir's login, not the proxy's shared credential. The credential-proxy launch agent is turned off (`launchctl bootout`, plist kept) at a session launch once no Claude session points at it, no connection is open on its port and the core has a fresh status line record, all read cleanly; until then it keeps running and the reason is logged. The intent is recorded per user before the bootout and reconciled on the next launch; nothing is signalled by PID. `src/startup.sh` no longer installs or starts the proxy while sessions go direct. `QUOTA_STATUSLINE_ENABLED=false` brings the proxy routing back: the next session launch starts the launch agent, or installs it if it never was, unless `CREDENTIAL_PROXY_ENABLED=false` (new, default `true`) says to keep the proxy off; sessions then go direct even if a proxy is still running.
- Codex core and Codex pool workers: **`codex app-server` is now the default** (the seat in place of the typed-into TUI), and the choice is persisted, so every launch honors it. `bash scripts/sutando-config.sh codex-app-server-select off` brings the TUI back (`on` returns to the seat); the choice is recorded (the desktop's `runtime.json` `codexAppServer`, else `core.codex_app_server` in the workspace config) and `codex-app-server` prints it; a non-empty `SUTANDO_CODEX_APP_SERVER` still overrides. See `docs/codex-core.md`.
- Sutando core: "switch account" in the owner's DM posts a core account card (`skills/account-switch`): the account in use (Codex or Claude core, masked), a "Use" button per account the desktop saved for a Codex core (restores it and restarts the core, then confirms in the DM), and "Add another account", which points to Settings so the sign-in code is pasted only in the app. No code or token is ever sent in chat.
- Codex core: `python3 src/codex_account.py` says which account a Codex home is signed in to (email and plan, from Codex's own `account/read`, else the email and plan claims of its `auth.json` id_token), so the core can answer "which account are you on?" instead of only "Logged in using ChatGPT". Prints no token. Documented in `docs/built-in-tools.md`.
- Model switch on a Codex core: `switch-model.sh <codex model>` and the model card now work on a Codex core instead of refusing (exit 4). The pick is the core's alone, recorded in `state/model-switch.json` with `runtime: codex` and never written to the shared Codex home, so pool workers keep their own model. An app-server seat core uses it from its next task (`turn/start` model); a Codex TUI core is told it is saved for its next start (exit 11), when the launcher passes it as `-m` unless `SUTANDO_CORE_MODEL` is set for that launch. The card lists the models Codex itself lists (`MODEL_SWITCH_CODEX_CHOICES` overrides). A Claude name on a Codex core is refused (exit 2).
- Sutando core: when the core runs out of usage (a Codex app-server seat's `usageLimitExceeded` turn, or a Claude Code core's usage-limit banner), the owner gets the core account card in their DM, once per limit, saying the limit was reached and when it resets if known; on a Claude Code core it replaces the "core is paused" notice for a usage limit, which still goes out for any other pause or when the card cannot be posted (`src/core_quota_notice.py`, `account_card.py post --owner-dm --lead`).
- Sutando core: the core's account health is kept in `state/core-account-health.json` (`ok` | `signed_out` | `quota`, the runtime, the account, `resets_at` for a limit) for Settings and the profile tab: the Codex seat sets `signed_out` when a login is refused even after a restart and `quota` on a usage limit, and `ok` again on the next completed turn or when the login on disk changes; the Claude Code core's monitor sets `quota` and `ok` for its usage-limit screen (`src/core_account_health.py`).
- Sutando core (Codex): the turn that applies a model switch no longer reports the model before it. The app-server seat tried the pick on the next task and wrote the result only when that task ended, so the task itself, running on the new model, read "pending" and answered with the old one. The record now carries a `running` mark from the moment Codex takes the turn with the pick, and the model card reads it; the pick is still confirmed only when that turn completes, and a turn that ends with no verdict clears the mark. `switch-model.sh` also names the model the core is on (the last one Codex took) in its "stays on" text, where it used to name the last pick saved.
- Sutando core: "switch to Claude Code" / "use Codex" in the owner's DM posts a core runtime card (`skills/runtime-switch`): it marks the runtime in use, checks the other runtime is signed in before stopping anything ("Sign in to <runtime> first" otherwise), restarts the core onto it after the current turn, and confirms in the DM from the launcher's confirmed core record and the desktop's selection.
- Sutando core: the runtime card's "Sign in first" answer no longer sends the owner to Settings and makes them ask twice. The card carries the sign-in controls for the runtime that was picked (drawn in the card by the desktop app on the computer that runs the core; elsewhere it says to open it there), the tap is kept, and once the sign-in is there the core switches by itself and confirms. If no sign-in comes within 15 minutes it says so and changes nothing.
- worker-pool: a worker that gets its first own s.space agent (a new worker's identity step, or `pool_identity.py add`, pasted or `--device-flow`) now moves to that agent's own task and result folders (`dirs: "own"`), as soon as the agent is saved and before its lane starts, so it answers as its own agent from the start. Work already delivered to it moves or is handed back as `worker_lane.py migrate-dirs --apply` does. `add --shared-dirs` opts out. Rotates, `provision-*`, and workers without their own agent keep their folders; `migrate-dirs` is for workers that already have an agent. A switch (by hand or on a first agent) now goes through `dirs: "migrating"`: the worker stays on its old inbox, and gets no new core task, until its delivered work has moved, and it waits while the worker still owes a task it accepted. A handler failure leaves it there instead of half-switched. `pool_manage.py retire` now counts a worker's unanswered tasks in its own folder, and `--hand-off` gives them to the core; the worker's agent row is removed only once that hand-off has succeeded (a failure leaves it retired with the row kept, for a re-run or `enable`). A switch and a retirement no longer interleave (one switch lock per worker), `own` is written only once the worker's lane has moved (`dirs: "committing"` before it), its own lane's tasks are never given to the core, and a trusted stop still reaches it mid-switch.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): owner and team-member Antigravity turns can create and edit Room Commons pages and run room actions as the agent itself: the Session gets the `ag2-space` MCP server as the agent, over stdio (never HTTP, where nothing filters the tools) through the desktop's `ag2-mcp-proxy` (`install --mcp-proxy-command`, descriptor from `ag2-sparrow-mcp descriptor`, new; tool names without dots through `ag2_sparrow.mcp_name_shim`, since agy drops dotted names), and the permission policy grants that server's room tools by server and tool name; the shim itself lists and forwards only those tools and answers any other `tools/call` with an error, so an agy that auto-allows MCP still cannot reach `relay.token.issue`, `agent.link`/`agent.unlink` or `space.action.execute` (still no shell, fetch or, for team, files). Guest turns get no S.space tools. ([#6653])
- Voice: a host can set what the core is asked to do after each voice call with `SUTANDO_VOICE_CALL_END_INSTRUCTION`. It replaces only the instruction sentences of the session-end task; the `VOICE_SESSION_ENDED:` facts and the spoken lines (the last 20,000 characters) stay. Unset or blank keeps today's text, byte for byte. A replacement must carry its own `[no-send]` rule.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): `install --allow-owner-shell-web` (off by default, recorded per agent) lets the owner's Antigravity turns run shell commands and fetch and search the web, as a local Claude Code agent does for its owner; without it every command, `execute`, `fetch` and `search` request is still refused, so existing installs do not change on update. The owner's file writes and edits under the working directory are no longer refused for agy's own argument names (`Content`, `Path`, `Edits`, ...: "unrecognised key Content"), on every install. Team and guest turns never get a command or web call, opt-in or not. Unknown operation kinds stay refused. ([#6656])
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): with `--allow-owner-shell-web`, an attested collaborator's turn on the owner's turn runs shell commands and fetches and searches the web like the owner's, matching what claude-local and codex-local give a collaborator; plain Team and guests stay without commands and web, and with the switch off nobody gets them. Risk: a collaborator with shell commands runs as the owner's account, so they can also read the agent's relay token file directly, and any other file or credential the owner can read; turn the switch on only for collaborators you trust with that. Upgrade effect: an install that already turned the switch on under #6656 (owner only) gives shell commands and web to its attested collaborators as soon as it upgrades, with no new prompt; to keep it owner-only, turn the switch off before upgrading (`uninstall`, then `install` without `--allow-owner-shell-web`; a repair `install --agent <id>` keeps the recorded switch on), or review the agent's collaborators first. ([#6675])
- Task watcher (task-watch Mod): the human owner's tasks that arrive while a turn is running now reach that turn after its next main-loop tool call, as a line attached to the tool's result, instead of waiting for the turn to end. Only `access_tier: owner` tasks from a person's channel with a non-agent sender qualify, read from envelope-verified headers by `src/task_watch_owner.py`; cron, health-check, API and other machine tasks keep the turn-end submit. A named task still pending when the turn ends is announced once more. The checks run as a task is announced, outside the hook, so a tool result is never held and Esc during a tool call loses nothing (the task is held, shown on the status line, and delivered after the person's next input); subagent tool calls never carry it, and any failure returns the tool's result untouched. ([#6643])
- ag2-sparrow: `ag2-sparrow-antigravity-local` hosts Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) on this computer as an s.space agent (`[antigravity]` extra): people @-mention it in a room and it answers there. Each task wakes `agy acp` over ACP, resumes the room's Session, and posts the turn's final message (`NO_REPLY` posts nothing); a non-owner's turn runs in its own temporary directory and agy home (`--gemini-dir`, deny-all rules, no global context), in a throwaway Session set to read-only (plan) mode, and is not run when agy offers no such mode; `install` refuses until agy is signed in, `verify` shows a `sign-in` row, and a task that finds agy signed out is answered with a line saying so. Handshake and sign-in check measured against agy 1.5.9; a signed-in turn is not yet checked live. The ACP turn, Session store, permission policy and task framing move from the OpenClaw adapter to a shared `ag2_sparrow/acp_host.py` (and `acp_client.py`); OpenClaw's prompts, permission verdicts and client name are unchanged.
- Codex core and Codex pool workers: the app-server seat runs on `codex app-server` instead of a TUI that a notifier types into. One process per seat (`src/agent/codex/app-server/seat.py`) keeps one durable thread and runs one turn per task with the notifier's prompt; the agent still writes its own result file. Approvals are declined, a Stop ruling sends `turn/interrupt`, and a dead app-server is restarted once with the task retried. No notifier or observer session is started for such a seat, and its terminal panel is a read-only log. Not yet in the seat: typing into the panel, slash commands, pane-based status and cards, model switch, mid-turn delivery. See `docs/codex-core.md`. ([#6651])
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): `install --resume-thread <uuid>` continues an existing Codex conversation (saved under `--codex-home`'s `sessions/`, as `codex resume <id>` takes it) in the owner's DM with the agent; it is resumed once, the first owner task in the DM, and every other room starts a new thread. An id with no saved conversation is refused before the token is read or anything is written. ([#6387])
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): `install` and `connect` take `--resume-session <uuid>` to host an existing Claude Code conversation instead of a new one. The id must name a transcript under the config dir's `projects/` that no running Claude Code process has open; otherwise nothing changes and connect's code is not spent. A kept id is replaced under the same proven-gone rule as `--new-session`; when it is not, the agent stays installed under the kept id and the command exits 79.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local): `install --agent <Matrix ID> --token-stdin` takes the agent's relay token pasted at a hidden prompt (or one piped line): the bare `<relay_url>|<secret>` token or a `REMOTE_TASK_TOKEN=` / `AG2_REMOTE_TOKEN='…'` line. It is written to the agent's seat as `connect` writes it (mode 600, never through a link), then install runs as with `--token-env-file`; the other adapter already serving the agent, or the agent's job still running, is refused before the token is read. ([#6263])
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local, codex-local): several agents per host, one job per agent. An agent installed on its own root runs as `ai.ag2.sparrow.<adapter>.<agent key>` (systemd `ag2-sparrow-<adapter>.<agent key>.service`), the key being its readable root segment, with its own bridge job, its config under `~/.config/ag2-sparrow/agents/<agent key>/`, claude-local's tmux socket in a short `~/.config/ag2-sparrow/run/<digest>/`, and its operation lock at `~/.config/ag2-sparrow/locks/<job>.oplock`, which nothing removes; `uninstall` removes the agent and run dirs once only its own files are left. `verify`, `uninstall`, `attach`, `stop` and `debug-run` take one selector (`--agent <Matrix ID>`, `--key <agent key>`, `--work <dir>` or `--single`), needed only when several jobs are installed; `install` checks one it is given; new `list` shows each job with its selector, and every command a line prints carries the selector that names exactly that job. A job an earlier release installed keeps its fixed name and is verified, reinstalled and removed as before. A job whose config is gone is recovered only from its own marked bridge unit or the declaration beside the root its unit records, and only when that declaration's agent is the one its root names (the bridge runtime's own rule); a declaration that cannot be read or proven the job's makes uninstall refuse and name its manual `rm`. The repair a line prints, `install <selector>`, reuses the job's recorded token file and flags, rewrites a config that no longer loads, and mints a new session id for a malformed one; an install's bridge starts only once its session holds the root, and is left stopped when it never does. A repair reads and runs nothing recorded until the record is proven that job's on its own root; every install, connect and uninstall of an agent, on either adapter, holds the agent's fence (`~/.config/ag2-sparrow/locks/agent.<agent key>.fence`) through the settle of the session it started; a failed install that leaves the session not running stops the agent's bridge too; printed `rm` lines are shell-quoted. One agent is still one bridge across adapters.
- Wedge probes: `src/wedge_probes.py` gives the shared wedge detector three pure signatures for the core seat (a live core with no ready task watcher and no standby, a `core-status.json` stuck on one step, and a prompt or sign-in only a person can clear), with the reason and what unblocks it. It publishes nothing itself; `report()` is the one hand-off to the detector. health-check's core-proactive-loop and core-supervisor rows now use the same rules.
- ag2-sparrow: `ag2-sparrow-hatch no-reply <result_file> [--reason TEXT]` ends a task with nothing posted and waits until Sparrow has settled it with the gateway (exit 0 settled, 1 not, 3 queued but not confirmed), and each owner task file says to end a task that needs no reply with a `[no-send]` result. ([#6128])
- ag2-sparrow: opt-in AgentActivity task lifecycle. `REMOTE_TASK_LIFECYCLE_V2=1` sends the lease `worker_id` and `execution_generation` on ack and results, beats each task on `/v1/tasks/heartbeat`, stops the core when the broker cancels or reclaims an attempt (withdrawn when a newer generation is acked here first; a newer attempt it stopped anyway is posted as failed); a task the broker closes, or cancels before the ack, leaves the inbox if the core has not taken it up, and the core is stopped if it has, and reconciles with `/v1/tasks/active`. An attempt nobody will answer stops beating and is posted as failed: its task file left the queue unanswered for 10 min (never dropped from flight as completed elsewhere), or the core took the queued file up and then wrote no turn activity or result for 30 min while the core is not mid-turn (2 h when its state is unknown). `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT=1` adds per-attempt turn files and gates each result on the turn's room actions. Both default off. ([#5883])
- ag2-sparrow: with `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT=1`, a task the owner answered resumes as a new turn carrying the answer as quoted room data, once per question episode, and each task file tells the agent to ask a blocking question with `room.question.ask` on its task id, sending any visible text with `room.message.send` first (its result file is not posted while the question is open). A wake's task file says it is a new turn of the task and must end with its own result. For a wake turn only (its file carries a `wake_episode:` header), the Stop hook does not count a result older than the queued file as its answer, and a turn that recorded a turn-ledger no-send loses the in-progress exemption, so the wake it left unanswered blocks; every other task is judged as before. A woken attempt is judged answered only by its own result, not the first attempt's archived reply, so a wake stopped or closed before the core takes it is withdrawn and a lost wake is failed. A question about the owner's own errand is asked in their DM, not a shared room, and a turn whose question's outcome was lost posts `waiting_input`, never its "I asked" note as the reply. The bridge's attempt records move to one ledger, `state/relay-task-ledger.json`: each broker effect (ack, result, cancel-ack) is claimed there before it is sent and committed after, and each newer generation or wake runs as a run of its own with its own result item, including a generation served after the earlier one finished (its answer refused as stale, say), which is held for its ack rather than taken for a redelivery. Its task file says whether the earlier attempt's answer was delivered, so the core answers again when it was not. The earlier `relay-task-attempts*.json` is ignored, so attempts in flight when the bridge is upgraded are not resumed. ([#5885])
- agent-activity: with `SUTANDO_STOP_INTERRUPT=1` (off by default; also the manifest's config), a Stop interrupts the core's running turn with one Escape when that turn is on exactly the stopped task, so a long tool call or a terminal prompt no longer delays the stop. The turn comes from Claude Code's own turn hooks (`UserPromptSubmit`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`): the tasks its prompt named and the dialog it is parked on. The key is fenced on that turn in the pane. A turn on several tasks, on another task, on no task, or one that cannot be read gets no key, and the Stop stays cooperative. The task shows `stop requested` until the stop is ruled: CANCELLED when the core answered the control task and wrote no result, left to delivery when it wrote a ready one (the shared readiness rules, a wake turn's own only), CANCELLED after an hour unanswered. The ruling survives restarts. Only a stop from the bridge's own control writer or the owner's local voice session (owner tier, in headers no body can forge) stops anything. A stop for a task a pool worker holds is routed to that worker's inbox, so the worker's own watcher interrupts and rules it, and the switch reaches each worker's watcher. Skills take a Stop through the new manifest field `on_stop_requested`; with none taking it (the switch off), a cancel marks the task CANCELLED at once, as before. With the switch on, a task the engine fails as stalled also gets a cooperative stop instruction. Cancel instructions and the agent-activity hook handle a gateway instance's `task-<instance>~task-<id>` as one id. ([#6089])
- ag2-sparrow: with `REMOTE_TASK_TURN_CONTEXT=1`, a task that asks this agent a room question carries the question as quoted, secret-redacted room data, and owner tasks are told to answer it once with `room.question.answer`, deciding from what `room.question.inspect` returns. The turn gate ignores outcomes about another task, so answering never parks or closes the agent's own task. An answer is matched to its question in the journal; a question answered here, or whose answer cannot be told, is never offered again, and the record of it is kept until the question expires. ([#6092])

## Fixed
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): stopping or restarting the agent's session leaves tmux copy mode before sending `/exit`. A scroll in a terminal viewing the session (the app's terminal tab) left the pane in copy mode, where `/exit` was swallowed and the stop came back uncertain.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): after an upgrade the agent's Claude Code session loads the ag2space-inbox plugin of the new ag2-sparrow. It kept loading the plugin of the version it was first installed with while that older environment was still on disk.
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): a local Codex agent whose login Codex itself refused (unauthorized even after a restart) says on its account card that its sign-in here no longer works, and the app offers to sign in again; asked later, the card said "I'm not signed in" or named the account still read from the refused login. The refusal is kept against that login file only, so any new sign-in clears it, and a login file alone is never called lapsed. ([#6832])
- account-switch (Codex core): a saved account that a local Codex agent on this computer keeps a login of its own for is no longer copied into the core; the switch says so, changes nothing, and points to signing in to that account instead. Two copies of one ChatGPT login end each other when either refreshes, so the core read "Codex isn't signed in anymore" within minutes of the switch. An agent that links the core's own login file shares it and does not count. The card's saved-account keys now follow the desktop's rule (workspace id and email), so a "Use" tap finds the account the desktop saved instead of answering that it is no longer saved. ([#6837])
- account-switch: the core's usage-limit card (Claude Code and Codex) says the limit and its reset alone; it added "The core (…) is not signed in." over the account it showed. Its account controls carry `limit`.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): a model picked on the agent's settings page while its session cannot take `/model` (a dialog or the usage-limit menu on screen, a start or a restart under way) is kept, and the session's next start runs on it; the page shows it as pending. It was refused with "the session does not show its whole input box".
- ag2-sparrow: a usage-limit account card (local Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) carries `limit` in its account controls, so the app's needs-you bar lists it as an agent out of usage, apart from an account menu the owner asked for.
- HITL cards: the engine now sends what came of an answer (`outcome`: running, done, failed with the driver's note, or a neutral closed for an answer a terminal driver sent and nobody saw take; a card no driver handles closes with its status alone, as before), so the web and iOS terminal cards show their result line; a terminal Yes/No dialog's buttons carry the terminal's own row text, so clients can number them. ([#6800])

- ag2-sparrow (bridge): a second bridge for an agent that is already being served on the same computer, from another folder or install, no longer polls: it says which process and folder hold the agent, reports it in the gateway status, and stands down. Two bridges polling as one agent each took tasks the other never saw.
- model-switch: two quick taps on the core's model card now end on the model tapped last. Each tap starts its own detached switch, in no fixed order; an older switch that ran last left the core on a model the card did not show (its outcome is superseded and never posted). Switches now run one at a time (`model_card.py turn`), and only the newest accepted attempt's switch runs.
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local, antigravity-local): asked which account it is on in the owner's DM ("which account are you using?", "agy account, can you see it?", "who are you signed in as?", "你用的哪个账号", "账号是什么"), the agent shows the account card instead of handing the question to the model, which cannot see its own sign-in and answered that it could not tell. "switch account" / "换账号" now does the same on local Codex without a turn. One rule (`account_switch.asks_for_card`), read by the card desk for every connector's account card; a message about some other account ("create an account on GitHub") or a longer request is still the model's.
- Cards: the account, model and runtime card sent in answer to an owner's message is now posted under an operation id derived from that message, not the current second, so a task retried after the card went out but before its result was written (a watcher restart) gets the earlier post back from s.space instead of a second card. A card answering nothing (the quota card) still posts anew each time.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): a message with another site's `?code=` link (a GitHub device-login link) or a path like `docs/4/...` is no longer refused as a sign-in code; an answer that opens with the term ("RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED is the gRPC code...") and another site's 429 in a failed turn's error are no longer taken for agy's usage limit; a collaborator who asks while agy is at its limit is told so, where they got no reply.
- Workers with identities on several connections share one stable task/result folder. Only the primary connection’s worker lane adopts shared results; room-addressed notes use the matching server’s lane, and stay undelivered when no identity serves that server. Changing the primary leaves the inbox in place. ([#6384])
- A decision card asked by a pool worker that has its own s.space agent is posted by that worker's agent in its own DM with the owner, titled with the worker's name, and the owner's click comes back to that worker. Before, the core's gateway tried to post it as the core, was refused, and the failure surfaced in the core's DM.
- quota-tracker: with status line tracking on (as the launchers decide it) and nothing still using the credential proxy (no established connection on its port, no live session carrying its URL), health-check no longer reports a running but out-of-date (or credential-exhausted) proxy as an issue: the row is `ok` with that state as information. The `claude-sign-in` check now uses the launchers' own routing predicate, so an empty `QUOTA_STATUSLINE_ENABLED` means the proxy there too. The `claude-sign-in` check treats a timed-out probe as unknown (no daily message), probes config dirs concurrently (four at a time), and removes its daily message markers after 7 days.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): a plugin reload inside a live session no longer loses the task the agent is working on. The reloaded plugin started with no memory of its tasks in flight, so the turn already running had its `ag2space_reply` refused ("not a task this session received") and the sender got an interrupted notice or nothing. The plugin now keeps its offers in the session's state, which a reload leaves in place, and takes them back at its next start when the CLI's new read-only `inbox inflight` still lists them as this generation's open claims at the same attempt: a queued prompt is still confirmed by its own turn, a running turn still answers, an accepted answer is published. A taken-back turn whose end was not seen is closed when the next main-loop turn starts, or after 30 minutes. Anything not kept or not listed fails closed as before. A reload at the edges is bounded too: a prompt not known to have reached the session is never resubmitted and does not hold intake, one that did is waited for five minutes, a confirmation being retried is retried after the reload, and the answer handed to `stage` is kept before the CLI is asked so a reload mid-stage still delivers it.
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): a local Claude Code agent whose model was switched (`ag2-sparrow-claude-local model <name>`, #6679) starts again afterwards. The switch leaves `state/model-switch.json` and `state/model-switch.lock` in the agent's work root, and the start check, which names every entry an agent's state may hold, did not name them: the next start of the job was refused with "state/model-switch.json is not this adapter's state". Both are now named, and the record's temp file is named so that one left by a stop is swept, not refused. The same refusal met an agent that had answered a guest on its isolated turn, which keeps its hourly cap in `state/isolated-turns.json`; that name is allowed too. The record is now written through the adapter's exclusive durable writer, and a `model-switch.json.tmp` left by the released writer is removed at the next start (a plain file only).
- Cards: a tap on a card from a core on the env (legacy) connection, which records no lane (the model card, worker approval and others), was answered "I couldn't match that button to a card I sent" and nothing happened. `agent_card.py click` now takes such a card's owner from the legacy connection row instead of treating the owner as unknown.
- Model switch (core skill): a switch to a 1M model (`sonnet[1m]`, `fable[1m]`) that Claude Code 2.1.322 answers without naming the context size ("Set model to Sonnet 5.5 and saved as your default for new sessions") was reported as not accepted (exit 8) although it happened. It now counts when that line is new and the core's `settings.json` was saved after the send naming exactly that model; the line alone, or a setting saved before the send, still does not.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): images and files people send now reach Antigravity: images as ACP image blocks in the prompt (when agy declares `image`), and on the owner's turn a read-only copy of the task's own files in a folder agy may read (`additionalDirectories`) but never change; an isolated non-owner turn gets the images only. The owner's final message keeps its delivery markers (`[channel:]`, `[thread]`, `[file:]` for a file under the working directory only), as Claude Code and Codex results do; non-owners' markers stay neutralised. A bridge launched without `REMOTE_MEDIA_MARKER` (the desktop's and connect's seat bridges) now resolves the AG2 Space gateway's `[ag2space-media: …]` marker too, so its download reaches every local adapter.

<!-- fix() PRs go here -->
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): "Switch account" and the saved-account menu on the account card were refused for every agent installed as its own job ("this agent shares its Claude config dir with another agent"). The check listed the other agents' configs from the single-agent job's path, so an agent whose config sits under `agents/<key>/` found its own config among them and matched its own folder. It now excludes the config of the job that serves the agent. Two agents that really share one folder are still refused; an agent two jobs serve is refused as not known.
- quota-tracker (credential proxy): the proxy no longer puts the core's requests on the machine's shared `claude` login. The launchd job is now installed with the core's own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (resolved through `claude-sutando-config-dir`, as startup does) instead of the installing shell's value or its `~/.claude` default, and `is-current` compares against that, so a job already loaded with another dir is reinstalled on the next startup. With a config dir set, the proxy injects, refreshes and retries only within that dir's own keychain item: when the item is missing, or its token is rejected or expired and cannot be refreshed, a request that carries its own credential is forwarded untouched and one without gets a 401; the shared `Claude Code-credentials` item is never used in its place (it still serves installs with no config dir). The proxy still records quota headers. It logs which keychain service it selected once at start and on change, warns once while the scoped item is missing or unusable, and no longer writes `security`'s "could not be found" line on every request (other keychain read failures are logged once). ([#6647])
- Sutando core (Codex): a "Use <account>" tap on the core account card from the web or a phone switches the core to that saved account, as a tap in the desktop app does: the tap carries only the choice and the saved sign-in never leaves the computer that runs the core. A tap message acts once (a client resending it on reconnect starts no second switch), each tap's outcome is one line in the owner-action audit (`state/recovery/audit.jsonl`, ids only), and "Add another account" says it needs the computer that runs the core.
- Stop hook (`check-pending-tasks.sh`): the core's block lists the owner's own messages first (owner tier, from a channel a person types or speaks into, not sent by an agent), ahead of `task-cron-*` files and team or agent tasks that glob order used to put before them; among the owner's messages, urgent before normal before low, then oldest first. Every other task keeps its place, and which tasks are listed is unchanged. Team and agent tasks now wait while the owner has a message pending. ([#6644])
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): the owner can change Antigravity's model from their DM with it, with nothing restarted. Asking it there in one's own words ("can you change model"), or sending `/model`, posts a card with a button per model agy offers; a tap records the pick and a card says the switch comes with the next message; each of the owner's turns then sets it on the Session (`session/set_model`) before the prompt, and after the first such turn a card in that DM says "Switched. I'm now using X.", or that the switch was refused and which model is still in use. Only the owner's tap on a card this agent posted, in that DM, acts. Under it, `connector_cards`: a connector queues an agent panel card for its bridge to post and judges the click with the core's own `agent_card` (now bundled with `issued_cards` and `local_record`). The ACP calls are the protocol's shapes and are not yet measured against a signed-in agy.
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): the owner can change local Codex's model from their DM with it, by the same card as Antigravity's. `/model`, or asking in one's own words, posts a card with a button for each of the first six models `model/list` offers and names the rest (`/model <name>` picks any of them); the pick goes on `turn/start` of every later turn on the kept threads (never a guest's ephemeral turn), and after the first such turn a card in that DM says it switched, or, when the turn failed or Codex reported moving it to another model, that it did not and the pick is dropped. Picking the model in use answers "already using". The card logic moved to a shared `model_switch` module that both connectors use; it is off, and the model is told nothing about it, for an agent without its own bridge. Not yet run against a signed-in Codex.
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): the owner can switch the account local Codex is signed in with from their DM with it. `/account`, or asking in one's own words, posts a card naming the account in use (the address shortened to its first letter and domain, and the plan) with a "Switch account" button. A tap starts a ChatGPT sign-in on the connector's own app-server (`account/login/start`), opens its page in the browser of the computer the agent runs on, and posts a card with a link to that page; when the server reports the sign-in over, a card in that DM says "Signed in" with the account now in use, or that it did not finish and which account is still in use. A sign-in nobody finishes is cancelled after ten minutes, and a new tap cancels the one before it. Cards a connector queues between two bridge sweeps are now posted in the order they were queued. A connector's cards are routed by a shared `card_desk`. Not yet run against a signed-in Codex, and no sign-in page has been opened by it outside the tests' stand-in.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local, codex-local, claude-local): the desktop app's agent settings page switches a local agent's model. `ag2-sparrow-antigravity-local model [--set <id>] --agent <id>` and `ag2-sparrow-codex-local model [--set <id>] --agent <id>` print `{current, available, pending, refused}` as JSON and record the owner's pick in the same `state/model.json` the model card keeps (`ag2_sparrow/model_settings.py`); every next turn runs on it, the owner's and a collaborator's (agy: `session/set_model`; Codex: `turn/start`'s `model`). `current` is what the connector saw run, and a pick stays `pending` until a turn used it. A page pick names no DM, so its outcome is settled without a card (`model_switch.tell`). `ag2-sparrow-claude-local model` also prints `current`, `available` and `pending`, and a restarted session starts on the model its last switch landed on (`--model`). Codex lists its models only once asked, so until then the page offers the card's allowlist.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): the model shown in agent settings and on the model card stays the owner's pick after the switch. A new Session opens on agy's default model before `session/set_model` moves it, and that opening report overwrote `current` in `state/model.json` on the turns after the switch, so the page went back to the default while turns ran on the pick. With a pick in force `ModelSwitch.seen` no longer takes `current` from the opening report; `tell` records the model the turn ran on when it differs (`ag2_sparrow/model_switch.py`).
- ag2-sparrow (claude-local): `ag2-sparrow-claude-local model [<model>] [--confirm]` prints the model its last switch landed on as JSON (`null` when it has made none; it does not read Claude Code's config dir), or switches the running session's without a restart. It types Claude Code's own `/model <model>` into the session through the same fenced sender `stop` uses (nothing is typed when the pane is not the recorded one), and reports `switched` only when the pane shows a new "Set model to" line; Claude Code's confirm dialog inside a running conversation is answered once with `--confirm` and cancelled without it. Accepts `default`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable` or a `claude-*` id, with an optional `[1m]` tag. Meant for a model control in the desktop app; the session's settings are still Claude Code's to write.
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): Antigravity takes its tier from the shared `task_io.turn_policy` like every other adapter, and only maps the verdict to a turn: owner and an attested collaborator get the owner's turn (working directory, agy's own home, the owner's read/edit policy, a Session of their own per room), restricted (guest, plain team, unknown tier) the isolated read-only turn, refused the refusal line. An attested collaborator no longer needs `--allow-non-owner` and is no longer answered isolated; `--allow-non-owner` still parses and changes nothing. Commands and the web stay the owner's only. A restricted turn may now read the files its sender attached to that task, and only those: they are copied read-only into the isolated working directory and only reads of those copies are granted; any other path, another task's attachment, a symlink or an oversize file is refused. ([#6674])
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): a Codex turn that completes without a message now says what it did instead (approvals not given, commands run, file changes, tool calls, web searches; a command, file change or tool call that failed is said to have failed, one that was declined is not said to have run, and only this turn's approvals are counted), where it used to post only `[no reply] Codex completed the turn without a message.` ([#6673])
- ag2-sparrow (codex-local): a restricted turn (a guest, plain team) can no longer read files outside its own temp folder. Codex's `read-only` sandbox stops writes and the network but not reads, so such a turn could read the owner's files; its thread now starts under a permissions profile that allows the turn's folder and what Codex needs to run, and a thread that is not confined fails the turn. ([#6670]) A restricted turn is also not started when Codex's `config/read` answer does not carry `config.mcp_servers` as a mapping: a server list that cannot be read is never taken as empty, which would leave the owner's MCP servers enabled. A restricted turn's own attachments are now opened from a descriptor on the bridge's media folder, one path component at a time and through no symlink, so the file copied is under that folder even if a path component is replaced meanwhile (claude-local and codex-local).
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): a person with Collaborator access (s.space's Team tier: the broker's `collaborator: true` stamp on the team tier, read from the task headers, never the message text) is now answered without `--allow-non-owner`, as codex-local and the OpenClaw connector already do, and gets the owner's turn: the working directory, agy's own home and the owner's permission policy (read or edit under the working directory; no command, no fetch), with a Session of their own per room, on the owner's agy sign-in (owner decision, 2026-11-21; this reverses #6616's collaborator opt-in). Before, every non-owner got "This agent only answers its owner here." A guest (any other sender, the team tier without the stamp included) is still refused unless `--allow-non-owner`, and is then served isolated and read-only as before: its own temporary directory and agy home with deny-all rules, a new Session never stored, agy's plan mode, no file operation or command granted. `verify` prints one `INFO team (attested collaborator)` and one `INFO guest` line. ([#6645])
- ag2-sparrow (antigravity-local): guests, plain team and unknown tiers are answered, as Sutando answers them, in the isolated read-only (plan) turn, without `--allow-non-owner` (now a no-op kept so existing configs parse); a wire `team` without the collaborator stamp stays a guest. The gateway's Sutando tier block reaches agy said as it can follow it: "your final message" instead of writing `results/<task>.txt`, and "this turn is the read-only sandbox" instead of `codex exec`, with the scope, DO / DO NOT lists, trust boundary and owner hand-off verbatim. ([#6659])
- Voice / task watcher (task-watch Mod): the low-priority task a voice session leaves when it ends is no longer treated as a message from the owner. `submitVoiceSessionEndTask` now writes it with `interaction_type: system_event` (as the phone call-end summary already is) instead of `realtime_audio`, and `src/task_watch_owner.py` answers not-owner for a `system_event`. This changes #6643 as merged: an end-of-call task no longer reaches a running turn after its next tool call; it waits for the turn to end like other machine tasks. A live voice request is unchanged. ([#6648])
- ag2-sparrow: the AG2 Space gateway decides a task's effective tier and whether the collaborator engage rulebook applies through one shared helper (`_sender_tier_and_collaborator`), instead of a private copy of the same formula in `_write_task`; a delivery that asks for team tier but whose broker attestation did not (yet) promote it to collaborator — the signature a cross-homeserver collaborator-attestation lag leaves on the wire — is now logged by sender, room and task id at the point it is served as guest, instead of being diagnosable only by diffing a task's `timestamp:` header against its file mtime after the fact. A relay adapter's `refusal()` also gives a Team-tier sender not yet attested as a collaborator its existing retry/backoff budget before the refusal becomes final, instead of refusing on sight like a guest — a real, narrower fix than the #5878 incident itself, which this does not close: the incident's actual wire shape (`access_tier: guest`, `requested_access_tier: team`) never reaches the Team-tier branch this covers, since the gateway resolves that combination to `guest` before a relay adapter ever sees it. ([sonichi/sutando#5878] investigation, not a fix for it)
- Task watcher (task-watch Mod): a task that arrived while a turn was running, and was answered before that turn ended (the Stop hook hands it to the model), is no longer announced again when the turn ends. Right before each submit the Mod asks `src/task_disposition.py` about every held task and announces only the ones still `pending`; the `QUEUE:` lines and the `N tasks waiting` status line count only what is left, and with nothing left no prompt is submitted. A check that fails or times out keeps the task: it is announced as before, and the trail says so. ([#6642])
- Task watcher (task-watch Mod): task delivery no longer stops for the rest of the session when a prompt submit never settles, and an announcement is no longer lost when Claude Code accepts a submit but starts no turn for it (seen after an interrupted turn): it is kept and sent again until a main turn starts with it. After the person interrupts a turn (Esc), Claude Code takes no plugin input until they type, by design; the Mod now holds the tasks, shows `N tasks waiting — type anything to resume` on the status line with one toast, and delivers them once after the person's next turn. A subagent's turn no longer counts as the session going idle. Deliveries are now recorded in `<workspace>/logs/task-watch-mod.log`, and each watcher start in `<workspace>/logs/watch-tasks-stream.log`. ([#6639])
- Task watcher: every dispatch decision after the task-handler probe now logs one line naming the probe's exit code and the outcome (announced, handled, or held with the live watcher that holds the claim), so a task that is neither announced nor run is never silent. Each catch-up pass also re-dispatches a task still in the inbox a pass later that this watcher never admitted and that is neither held nor answered, so a drop with no known cause heals within two passes.
- ag2-sparrow: a proactive message's `[file:]`/`[send:]`/`[attach:]` attachment is uploaded to the room the message went to, after the message is delivered; a refused file is logged by name, and a message that is only an attachment sends "(file attached)" instead of waiting forever. A re-published message whose attachment changed (another file, or new bytes under the same path) is a new send. A redirected message whose body the destination guard withholds uploads none of its files, and a non-owner room's logs name only the file name. (#4193)
- ag2-sparrow: the `ag2-sparrow-outbox` recovery command logged for a quarantined result names its `--root` and `--results-dir` through the workspace resolver (`$HOME` without one) and quotes its ids, so the log carries no home path and a workspace path with a space no longer splits the command. ([#6447])
- schedule-crons: the seeder's owner notices (a restored `crons.json`, legacy jobs not enabled) are recorded before the schedule is written, queued once to the owner's DM through the proactive outbox, and kept, printed at most once a day, until `seed_crons.py --notice-sent`; a failed legacy backup or notice write no longer loses them. ([#6448])
- ag2-sparrow: the requeue command the bridge logs for a parked message names its outbox root through `bash scripts/sutando-config.sh workspace` (or `$HOME` when no workspace resolver is set), so the log no longer carries a home path; run it from the engine checkout as before. ([#6445])
- Core limit hold: a 429 whose own response reports the account's limits all allowed no longer pauses the core ("rate limit on claude-fable-5-2" while the account had quota); it holds only when its text names a usage limit or a retry time. The credential proxy now records each rejection's own rate-limit headers (`limit_headers`), and only those count; a 429 without them keeps the backoff. The CLI's "(not your usage limit)" throttle error no longer pauses it either, and its "You've reached your Fable limit" now holds as a usage limit on the model the banner names, whatever model ran the turn before.
- hitl: a card first posted through one homeserver and revised after the agent moved to another (the s.space cutover) no longer stops every other card. The new relay answers the status edit with HTTP 404 because it does not hold the original message; the projector took that for a missing endpoint, retried the same edit on every pass and never reached the cards behind it, so permission and decision prompts did not arrive. An edit refused with 404 is now sent as a new card, which later revisions edit; a 404 for that send, or any other refusal of the edit, is handled as before. ([#5994])
- schedule-crons: a missing `hosts/<host>/crons.json` is no longer self-healed from the in-checkout `skills/schedule-crons/crons.json`, so a fresh or relabelled host no longer starts the sample digest and the morning briefing without the owner opting in. The new `scripts/seed_crons.py` seeds the template without its `"opt_in": true` entries, never reseeds a host whose file existed before from an older copy, and keeps a legacy file's own jobs aside in `crons.legacy.json`, named for the owner, unregistered. `src/init.sh` no longer writes the in-checkout file. ([#6443])
- ag2-sparrow: the bridge's `poll network error` and `poll recovered` lines add how much of a poll gap the host was awake (`868s since last successful poll, 35s of it awake`) when it slept through part of it, so a sleeping Mac no longer reads as a poll hung for minutes. An awake gap logs as before. ([#6439])
- hitl: a card whose room refuses the agent (HTTP 403 "sender is not in this room") no longer holds back the cards behind it: it waits out its own backoff and, after `ROOM_REFUSAL_ATTEMPTS` (5) sends, is marked failed for that revision and logged, instead of being retried every pass under a 60 s bridge backoff with no limit. Its failure notice, refused by the same room, is recorded once and not re-sent. Any other 403, and every other refusal, is handled as before. ([#5054])
- hitl: when a runtime prompt card's room refuses the agent, the card's failure notice (and any reminder) now goes to the owner's DM instead of being dropped, so the owner learns the card failed. A DM that refuses it too is recorded once and not retried. ([#5054])
- ag2-sparrow: a withheld non-owner result whose private review DM answers HTTP 403 "sender is not in this room" gets `ROOM_REFUSAL_ATTEMPTS` (5) sends spaced 2 s doubling, then the same review is sent once to a new private room that later reviews use, instead of being re-sent to the refusing room on every 1 s scan. If the new room refuses too, the review is logged as dropped with its record's path. Any other 403 is retried as before. ([#5054])
- ag2-sparrow: a relay ask that repeats an earlier one from the same person in the same room folds into it (`[deduped:]`) instead of being reported as "The holder's delivery destination or sender could not be verified". The bridge writes the ask's `asked_by` above `task:`, and `asked_by` joins the task header vocabulary. A fold between different askers or rooms, or of an ask with no room, is still refused.
- worker-pool: a pool worker that has its own agent sends its proactive notes (for example the owner line after a room join) as that agent, from its own lane, into that agent's owner DM: `result_publish.py` stamps a worker session's proactive file `proactive-<ts>.by-<worker>.txt`, only that worker's lane claims it, and no core lane or other bridge does. The worker seat's `s-space` MCP proxy mints from the worker's own vault credential through `scripts/connections.py worker-mcp-credential` (`AG2_MCP_WORKER_CREDENTIAL`), never the core's; a worker with no enabled identity of its own keeps acting through the core in both.
- Tests: a test that runs an agent with `SUTANDO_TEST_MODE=1` (the spawned voice-agent suites, for one) no longer shows real desktop notifications on the machine running it. The notify helper (`src/platform.ts` and its Python twin `src/sutando_platform.py`) writes the banner to stderr instead of calling osascript, PowerShell or notify-send. Production, which never sets the variable, is unchanged. ([#6219])
- Voice: after a region refusal, voice comes back as soon as the network route is fixed. Retry on the error card (or the mic button) asks Google again and connects on that attempt, instead of showing the earlier refusal again, and a client that stays connected is redialed on the normal schedule (1 s, rising to 60 s) instead of waiting 5 minutes. While Google still refuses, the region message is shown as before. Other terminal failures (credits, quota, key, model) keep the 5-minute hold. ([#6218])
